prTitle: Improve time complexity and reduce memory allocations

interpretation.changeDescription: Optimized the `resolveToolDefinitions` method in `DefaultToolCallingManager` by pre-calculating a `Set` of existing tool names from `chatOptions.getToolCallbacks()` before iterating through the requested tool names.
interpretation.changeMotivation: The original implementation performed a stream-based check (`anyMatch`) inside a loop for every tool name being resolved. This resulted in an O(N*M) time complexity (where N is the number of tool names and M is the number of existing tool callbacks). By using a `Set` for lookups, the complexity is reduced to O(N+M), improving performance when dealing with a large number of tool callbacks.

content.motivation: The change optimizes the tool resolution process by replacing an O(N*M) nested loop (stream-based lookup) with an O(N+M) approach using a HashSet, significantly improving performance when managing a large number of tool callbacks.
content.suggestion: Refactor the pre-calculation of tool names to use a traditional loop to improve readability and avoid the overhead of Stream API and object allocation for small collections. Include null checks when extracting tool names to ensure robustness.
goodPoints: Correctly identifies and implements the algorithmic complexity improvement from O(N*M) to O(N+M).
Effectively leverages a HashSet for constant-time lookups during the iteration process.
badPoints: Unnecessary defensive copying of the toolCallbacks list causes extra memory allocation.
The use of Stream API for a simple mapping to a Set introduces unnecessary abstraction and overhead for small lists.
The code lacks defensive programming against potential null values returned from tool definitions, which could cause NullPointerExceptions.

implementationDetails.details: The implementation introduces a HashSet for lookups. To improve efficiency and safety, consider replacing the current Stream-based collection with a simple for-each loop, pre-sizing the HashSet to the size of the callback list, and adding a null check for `tool.getToolDefinition()` and its name.

draft.title: Redundant defensive copy of toolCallbacks list
draft.description: The code creates a new ArrayList by wrapping chatOptions.getToolCallbacks(). This creates an unnecessary memory allocation since the list is only used to populate the 'existingToolNames' Set and for potential iteration. If the original list is immutable or can be iterated directly, the copy is wasteful.
draft.assumption: chatOptions.getToolCallbacks() returns an iterable or list that does not require defensive copying for thread safety or modification.

verdict.reason: The issue is confirmed because the code explicitly creates a defensive copy of chatOptions.getToolCallbacks() using new ArrayList<>(chatOptions.getToolCallbacks()), which is unnecessary if the original list is already iterable and does not require defensive copying. The code then uses the stream to collect tool names into a Set, which is only used for lookup via contains(), making the copy redundant. There is no evidence of thread safety or modification risks, and the original list is not modified elsewhere.
evidence: The code creates a defensive copy with new ArrayList<>(chatOptions.getToolCallbacks()) at line 103, which is unnecessary if the list is already iterable.
The code collects tool names into existingToolNames set using stream().map().collect(Collectors.toSet()) for containment checks via contains(), which does not require a defensive copy.
No thread safety or modification concerns are indicated in the code or project context.

draft.title: Stream chain complexity in pre-calculation
draft.description: The Stream API is used to map tool names into a set. While concise, this is a multi-step transformation that could be more readable as a simple loop if the performance gain of the Set is the only goal.
draft.assumption: The project prefers readable, imperative code over compact stream chains.

verdict.reason: The issue is confirmed because the project uses a stream chain to collect tool names into a set, which is a multi-step transformation that could be more readable as a simple loop. The project's preference for readable, imperative code over compact stream chains is a clear assumption, and there is no existing mechanism that mitigates this complexity. The code is reachable and not temporary, so the risk of reduced readability is real.
evidence: The code uses a stream chain to collect tool names into a set (existingToolNames), which is a multi-step transformation.
The project's assumption is that readable, imperative code is preferred over compact stream chains.
The loop is used to check if a tool name is already present, which is a direct result of the set created by the stream chain.

draft.title: Potential NullPointerException in stream
draft.description: If tool.getToolDefinition() or tool.getToolDefinition().name() returns null, the Stream collector will fail or the resulting Set will contain nulls, potentially causing unexpected behavior in the later 'contains' check.
draft.assumption: The tool definition or its name could be null based on existing API contracts.

verdict.reason: The code change introduces a stream operation that collects tool names into a Set, but it does not handle the possibility that tool.getToolDefinition().name() could return null, which would cause the Stream to produce a null value and potentially lead to a NullPointerException when the Set is used in the subsequent contains() check.
evidence: The code uses stream().map(tool -> tool.getToolDefinition().name()) which will return null if getToolDefinition().name() is null.
The resulting Set may contain null values, which would cause unexpected behavior in the contains() check.
The Stream collector does not filter out null values, and the Set may contain nulls, leading to potential NPE when checking toolName against the Set.

draft.title: Unnecessary intermediate object creation for Set
draft.description: Using Stream.collect(Collectors.toSet()) allocates a temporary Set object for every method call. For small lists of tool callbacks, this allocation might be more expensive than the O(N*M) linear search it intends to replace.
draft.assumption: The typical number of tool callbacks is small (e.g., < 10).

verdict.reason: The issue is confirmed because the code explicitly creates a temporary Set object using Stream.collect(Collectors.toSet()) for every method call, which is unnecessary when the number of tool callbacks is small. The existing code does not have any mechanism to avoid this allocation, and the assumption that the number of callbacks is small (<10) is reasonable given the context of tool callbacks, which are typically limited in number. The optimization to use a Set for containment checks is valid and reduces the O(N) search to O(1), but the temporary Set allocation is still a performance concern.
evidence: The code uses Stream.collect(Collectors.toSet()) to create a Set<String> for each call to resolveToolDefinitions, which allocates a temporary object.
The assumption that tool callbacks are small (<10) is reasonable and supported by the context of tool callbacks in a chat application.
No existing mechanism avoids the temporary Set allocation, and the code does not use a pre-allocated Set or other optimization.

draft.title: Encapsulation leak regarding tool names
draft.description: The logic to extract names from tool definitions is repeated. This logic should ideally be encapsulated within the tool callback interface or a helper class to avoid exposing the internal structure of tool definitions to the manager.
draft.assumption: The structure of ToolDefinition might change in the future.

verdict.reason: The issue describes a repetition of logic for extracting tool names from tool definitions, which is now mitigated by using a Set to store existing tool names via a stream operation. This change eliminates the need for repeated calls to getToolDefinition().name() and avoids exposing internal structure, as the set is built once and reused. The assumption that ToolDefinition structure might change is addressed by the use of a stream and a Set, which are robust to such changes. No encapsulation leak remains because the internal logic is encapsulated within the resolveToolDefinitions method.
evidence: The code now uses a Set<String> existingToolNames built from a stream of tool names, which is more efficient and encapsulates the logic.
The loop checks existence via existingToolNames.contains(toolName), avoiding repeated calls to getToolDefinition().name().
The imports were updated to use Java 8+ features (stream, Collectors), which are standard and do not expose internal structure.
The original repeated logic with anyMatch and stream was replaced with a single stream operation to build the set.

draft.title: Comment describes what instead of why
draft.description: The comment inside the loop explicitly states it is skipping tools already present. Since the code now uses a Set lookup, the code is self-documenting; the comment adds clutter without providing additional architectural context.
draft.assumption: The team prefers clean code that avoids redundant comments.

verdict.reason: The comment in question is indeed redundant because the code now uses a Set lookup to check for existing tool names, making the purpose of the check self-evident. The comment adds no architectural context and only introduces clutter, which aligns with the team's preference for clean code. The code change has already mitigated the issue by removing the need for the comment.
evidence: The diff shows the removal of a loop with a manual stream check and the addition of a Set-based check (existingToolNames.contains(toolName)), which is more efficient and self-documenting. The comment is removed entirely, indicating it was deemed unnecessary. The code now relies on the Set for the check, eliminating the need for the explanatory comment.
